newsitem.title: USA: Boston cardiologist convicted of embezzlement jailed.
newsitem.headline: Boston cardiologist convicted of embezzlement jailed.

text.p: The former chief of cardiology at Boston's Children's Hospital began serving a prison sentence on Monday for embezzling more than $117,000 from the hospital, Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger said.

The state's highest court, the Supreme Judicial Court, denied an appeal from Dr. Bernardo Nadal-Ginard to reverse his 1995 conviction of embezzling $117,777 from the Boston Children's Hospital Heart Foundation.

Meanwhile Sotheby's was preparing to auction off his art collection -- valued at approximately $6 million -- for a prior civil court ruling that he improperly took millions from the foundation that he founded.

A jury found that the 53-year-old physician, who used to give tours of his art collection at his home in Boston's fashionable Back Bay neighbourhood, used the money that was meant to pay for research equipment for children with heart disease for his own personal expenses.

Nadal-Ginard was ordered to serve one year in prison and perform 40 hours of community service weekly upon his release. He was also given a suspended three- to five-year prison sentence and ordered to make restitution.

According to the American Medical Association, cardiologists who are surgeons earned an average of $278,700 in 1995, the latest year available. Those who are internists earned $185,700 for the same year.
"He had quite an extensive art collection," said Assistant Attorney General Carol Starkey.

The collection of contemporary artists, including works by Jeff Koons, Bruce Nauman and Gerhard Richter, was forfeited when a federal court ruled in December 1994 that Nadal-Ginard had abused his responsibility and acted in bad faith by improperly taking millions of dollars from the heart foundation that he had started in 1982.
The Boston Children's Heart Foundation is selling the collection through Sotheby's with the first sale at the New York branch in May and a second auction to be held in the London branch in June.
